subject: English Language
source: AQA GCSE English Language 8700 specification (2015 onwards). The course is a single tier; spec points map to Assessment Objectives (AO1–AO6) and the two papers (Paper 1: Explorations in creative reading and writing; Paper 2: Writers' viewpoints and perspectives). 'tier' is set to 'both' throughout because there is no Foundation/Higher split; pupils sit the same papers.

specPoints.specTitle: Paper 1 reading — identify and interpret explicit information and ideas in a 20th-century literature fiction text
Paper 1 reading — select and synthesise evidence from the text to support understanding
Paper 1 reading — explain, comment on and analyse how writers use language and structure to achieve effects (e.g. word choice, sentence structure, imagery, narrative perspective)
Paper 1 reading — evaluate texts critically and support this with appropriate textual references; the 8-mark evaluation question on the writer's methods
Paper 1 writing — communicate clearly, effectively and imaginatively in descriptive or narrative writing in response to a visual or written stimulus (24 marks for content and organisation)
Paper 1 writing — use a range of vocabulary and sentence structures for clarity, purpose and effect, with accurate spelling, punctuation and grammar (16 marks for technical accuracy)
Paper 2 reading — identify and interpret information across two non-fiction texts (one 19th-century, one 20th/21st-century) and synthesise findings
Paper 2 reading — analyse how the writer uses language to convey opinions, attitudes or arguments (12-mark question)
Paper 2 reading — compare writers' ideas and perspectives, and how these are conveyed across the two texts (16-mark comparison question)
Paper 2 writing — produce a transactional/persuasive piece (letter, article, speech, leaflet, etc.) on a given viewpoint topic (24 marks for content and organisation)
Paper 2 writing — accurate Standard English; varied vocabulary and sentence structures for impact (16 marks for technical accuracy)
Language techniques: simile, metaphor, personification, onomatopoeia, alliteration, sibilance, hyperbole, juxtaposition, oxymoron — identification and analysis of effect
Structural techniques: in medias res, flashback, foreshadowing, cyclical structure, withholding information, shifts in time/perspective/focus — identification and analysis of effect
Sentence forms: simple, compound, complex; minor sentences; varying sentence length for effect
Persuasive devices in non-fiction: direct address, rhetorical questions, anecdotes, statistics, expert opinions, emotive language, triplets/listing, repetition
Writing — planning a response: structuring across an introduction, development paragraphs and a satisfying ending; varying paragraph length for impact
Writing — building a sustained voice and register matched to form, audience and purpose
Writing — vocabulary precision: using ambitious word choices accurately and avoiding repetition
Writing — accurate punctuation: full stops, commas, semicolons, colons, dashes, brackets, apostrophes, speech marks; demarcating sentences accurately
Writing — accurate spelling of complex/ambitious words and consistent tense
